To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

learning analytics dashboards have been used to provide stakeholders with information on learner performance and engagement, that the design of these dashboards needs to be tailored to the needs of the stakeholders, and that there is a need for a theoretical framework that explains how dashboards can be used to support better sense making and decision-making.

learning analytics dashboards have a rich potential to support sense making, but that there is a need for more theoretical underpinnnings of the domain and more research on how to design dashboards for different stakeholders in the educational context.

learning analytics dashboards are a powerful tool for sense-making, decision-making and reflection, that they can be tailored to the needs of different stakeholders, that they should be designed in a participatory way and that they should be evaluated in real-life learning settings.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of visual representations of learning analytics data to support sense making and decision-making processes in learning contexts.

(a) understanding and modelling the decision making process of stakeholders; (b) developing visualisation and interaction techniques for dashboards that are sensitive to the needs of the stakeholders and the decision making process; and (c) developing theoretical models that can help explain the role of dashboards and visualisation for the decision making process.
the design and evaluation of dashboards that are able to support the human in making sense of and taking actions in complex learning situations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
learning analytics dashboards have been a key research topic for the past decade and will continue to play an important role for the future of learning and teaching.

the future of learning dashboards will be more human-centric, will focus more on the human in the loop, will be more multimodal and more adaptive, will be more participatory, and will be more theory-driven.
the research community is currently at a stage where we have to start thinking about how to make learning analytics dashboards work in practice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we need to move from the current focus on data visualisation and data prediction towards a focus on the human and the social aspects of learning analytics dash-boards.
we need to understand the role of dashboards in learning analytics and how they are perceived by the various stakeholders.
the future of learning dashboard research should aim to (1) support the human sense-making process, (2) support human decision-making processes, and (3) be based on solid theoretical foundations.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the research community should continue to explore the use of participatory design methods in the development of learning analytics dash- boards, and that it should start to explore the use and value of learning analytics dash-board data for the development of machine learning techniques for educational recommender systems.

learning analytics dashboards have the potential to support better decision making in education, and we need to further develop our understanding of how they work, and how they can be designed and implemented to support the needs of the different stakeholders.
we need more research on the human aspects of dashboards and the use of dashboards in practice.
